title: Reckless high-speed street race on California highway ends with crash, overturn, ejection of driver - NewsBreak
text: MODESTO – A dangerous street race on State Route 99 in the Central Valley ended in a violent crash and an arrest, according to the California Highway Patrol’s Modesto office. CHP officers reported that the incident involved a Corvette and a Mustang engaged in reckless driving and racing on the busy highway. During the race, the driver of the Corvette lost control, veered off the shoulder, and overturned several times. The impact ejected the driver from the vehicle, causing major injuries. While emergency responders rushed to aid the Corvette driver, officers said the Mustang driver fled the scene and continued to their residence in Manteca. CHP Modesto officers later went to the Manteca address, where they arrested the driver. “This is a stark reminder that street racing is extremely dangerous,” CHP Modesto stated. “These dangerous behaviors put everyone at risk — drivers, passengers, and innocent bystanders.” Officials emphasized that “reckless driving isn’t just illegal — it’s deadly,” warning that “at highway speeds, a single mistake can cause a chain reaction with tragic consequences.” CHP urged drivers to keep racing off public roads and to act when witnessing unsafe driving. “Racing belongs on the track, not on public roads,” the agency noted. Authorities encouraged residents to call 9-1-1 if they see dangerous driving, but only when it is safe to do so. They also reminded motorists to obey posted speed limits, share the road responsibly, and remember that “aggressive driving is never worth the risk.”
